title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: In (35), Delta_infty^t is written {t ± sqrt(t(1-t))}. The roots of z^2 - 2tz + t are t ± sqrt(t^2 - t) = t ± sqrt(t(t-1)). This is a sign slip inside the root and has no effect on the rest, which only uses the quadratic equations.

Implicit gap: (36) asserts the multiplicities 2 and the form of f without proving that a V-equivariant/[2]-compatible map exists. The existence is supplied by the elliptic-curve origin, as the author notes on p. 62. Otherwise the computation of c_t = t is correct.

ideas.what: The Klein four-group of involutions of P^1 preserving {0,1,infty,t}, with explicit formulas and fixed-point schemes.
ideas.modern_name: Kummer line / V_4 action of 2-torsion translations on E/±1 (Legendre form)

ideas.what: Multiplication by 2 descended to P^1 as a degree-4 rational map: f_2^t(z) = t((z^2-2z+t)/(z^2-2tz+t))^2, with the origin's image at t.
ideas.modern_name: Lattès map of the Legendre family (duplication on the Kummer line)

ideas.what: Characterising [2] on the Kummer line purely in terms of the marked points J and t: f is the quotient by V, with fixed-point pairs sent to J. This works over any base S with 2 invertible.
ideas.modern_name: E/E[2] ≅ E via [2]; Kummer quotient P^1/V_4 ≅ P^1

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful, correct computation of a classical object: the Lattès/duplication map for the Legendre family, with the origin's image placed at t. It is presented as the quotient of P^1 by the Klein four-group fixing four points. The scheme-theoretic, base-independent framing is characteristic of Grothendieck, but the mathematics is well known.
transcription_corrections: The transcription faithfully reproduces Grothendieck's slip Delta_infty^t = {t ± sqrt(t(1-t))}; mathematically it should be sqrt(t(t-1)).
In the crossed-out fragment on the line computing f_2^t(zeta), the deleted expression appears to be 't^2 - 2t zeta + t^2 over zeta^2 - 2 zeta + 1'. It is struck through and irrelevant.
'c_t section de O_S^*' is correct; the image shows 'c_t section de O_S^*' after the displayed formula.
